units.text: INT. RIDESHARE - NIGHT
SUPER: "2:07 AM.
ROUTE 9.
NO STREETLIGHTS."
A battered hatchback, air freshener swinging, dashboard mounted phone glowing with a map that shows a road that does not exist on any other map.
Rain of a strange silver colour hangs in the headlights without falling.
Tobias Wren, 50s, driver, tired kind eyes, a thermos wedged between the seats, drives with one hand.
In the back seat sits the hooded passenger, THE WOMAN, face hidden, a long coat soaked at the hem, hands folded very still on a wooden box in her lap.
Next to her slumps Pip, 19, student, earbuds in, a backpack clutched like a pillow.
In the far seat is Hollis Grey, 60s, in a pressed suit, not touching the upholstery, and beside Tobias in the front sits Ines, 30s, a nurse in scrubs, scrolling her phone with a frown.
CLOSE ON the dashboard clock.
It does not change.
Everyone good back there? I can turn the heat up.
units.name: TOBIAS

units.text: Nobody answers.
THE WOMAN tilts her head, listening to something far away.
Your app says four minutes to Birchmont. We've been four minutes for twenty.
units.name: INES

units.text: Road's long tonight.
units.name: TOBIAS

units.text: ANGLE ON Pip pulling out an earbud, blinking at the window.
There's a tree out there. Same tree. Left side, three times now.
units.name: PIP

units.text: A man learns to stop counting trees.
units.name: HOLLIS

units.text: Okay, that's not a thing people say.
units.name: TOBIAS
paren: a short laugh that doesn't land

units.text: WE SEE the wooden box in THE WOMAN's lap.
A faint light seams its edges.
Her fingers tighten.
Ma'am? You okay? You haven't said anything since you got in.
units.name: INES

units.text: I have been saying it. You have not been listening.
units.name: THE WOMAN

units.text: INSERT - THE BOX
Carved into the lid: a small door, and a keyhole shaped like a crescent.
BACK TO SCENE
Tobias taps the brakes.
The car does not slow.
The silver rain begins to fall upward.
Tobias. Dude. The brakes.
units.name: PIP
paren: hands flat on the seat in front of him

units.text: I'm pressing them.
units.name: TOBIAS

units.text: She's come for the debt. It was always going to be tonight.
units.name: HOLLIS

units.text: What debt? Whose debt?
units.name: INES

units.text: THE WOMAN lifts her hood.
Her face is a girl's face, maybe sixteen, silver-eyed, tired, very old.
Hollis took the key from my mother. He promised to bring it back before the moon turned.
units.name: THE WOMAN

units.text: Mara. Please. I was young.
units.name: HOLLIS
paren: rising from the seat, bumping the roof

units.text: You were forty-one.
units.name: MARA
paren: opening the box, a pale blaze filling the car

units.text: The light swallows the dashboard, the map, the unmoving clock.
Tobias shouts.
Pip's earbud falls to the floor.
Ines grabs for the door handle and finds it gone.
CLOSE ON Hollis's hand, a crescent-shaped key trembling in his palm.
Take it. Take it and let them out.
units.name: HOLLIS

units.text: They were never held. Only you.
units.name: MARA
paren: taking the key, setting it in the lid

units.text: The car stops.
All at once.
The rain falls down again.
Silence.
The hatchback sits in an empty field under a normal moon.
The seat beside Mara is empty, a pressed suit folded neatly on the cushion.
Where did he go?
units.name: TOBIAS

units.text: Home.
units.name: MARA
paren: closing the box, stepping out into the grass

units.text: She walks away into the dark.
The dashboard clock finally clicks to 2:08.
